transcript:
Meeting start: 2026-01-12 14:00 PST
Duration 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Reyes, Priya Shah, Evan Cole - Redwood; Marcus Lin, Aisha Patel, Leo Gomez, Nina Romero - HalcyonWare

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE for Redwood Inference. we're here to scope the pilot, specifically security gates, residency and the throughput bench.
[00:12] Marcus: Hi all - Marcus here. building a doc automation product, heavy regs for EU data. need to verify logs, sso, and that PII never leaves region.
[00:21] Aisha: yes, from security side SOC2 is table stakes, ISO would be nice. we need audit logs for one year, and we have strict SAML requirements (Okta) and SCIM ideally.
[00:31] Priya: great, thanks Aisha. quick note - we can do hosted API for fast onboarding, Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC) for on-prem or strict residency. For the pilot we can stage dedicated in eu-west-1 and wire SAML.
[00:50] Leo: what's the realistic throughput we can test? our target for pilot is roughly 50 qps of inference at avg 400 tokens per request, and p95 latency under 700ms.
[01:01] Evan: ok, 50 qps at 400 tokens — that's a useful starting point. do you have a 95/99 target and budget for cost per million tokens for this pilot?
[01:12] Leo: we'd like p50 <200ms, p95 <700ms, and cost per 1M tokens ideally under $40 but we can flex for the pilot.
[01:20] Marcus: also, we run some peak bursts where qps spikes to 300 for a few minutes during batch ingests, so the bench needs spike tests.
[01:29] Priya: noted. We'll propose a benchmark plan: sustained load at 50 qps for 1 hour, spike storms to 300 qps for 5-10 minutes, and a long tail latency analysis. We'll run against a medium-size open model we recommend and also a quantized variant for Dedicated.
[01:41] Aisha: from the compliance side: can you support customer-managed KMS? We do not want keys managed by the vendor unless we hold the envelope key.
[01:50] Jordan: yes - Redwood supports KMS integrations and in Private deployments we can support customer KMS/HSM. For hosted we have bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options with envelope encryption; I'll send the KMS integration doc.
[02:02] Nina: for SSO, we need SAML 2.0 and SCIM for groups. Can you do role-based groups mapping to Redwood roles?
[02:11] Priya: we support SAML, and SCIM provisioning is supported for full pilot and for Dedicated. RBAC maps can be pre-seeded: admin, engineer, viewer. mapping and attribute rules are configurable. There's occasional naming mismatch in our older exports (Redwood console sometimes shows 'Redwood Dedi' in logs) — will ensure docs have canonical names.
[02:34] Aisha: audit logs — how granular are they? do we log full prompt text, or are prompts redacted? retention options?
[02:42] Evan: Audit logs capture request metadata, user/subject, model version, latency, token counts, and can optionally include full prompt payloads. For regulated POCs we typically redacted sensitive fields by default and can stream logs to customer SIEM (Splunk/Datadog). retention is configurable; for pilot we can set 12 months.
[03:00] Marcus: data residency enforcement — we need the inference and logs to stay in eu-west-1. how do you guarantee that?
[03:07] Jordan: we do region pinning for customer projects in Dedicated and Private. For hosted tier we can ensure region routing to eu-west-1 and country-level placement, with contractual clauses. For strongest guarantee we recommend Dedicated in the region or Private VPC.
[03:24] Leo: technical: what's the impact of KV cache on latency under load? some of our flows are long-context with repeated prefixes.
[03:33] Priya: KV cache helps reduce token compute on repeated prefixes and lowers p50 latency. In our bench we'll test with and without prefix caching; cache hit rates will factor into cost. We'll also measure token generation per second and GPU utilization.
[03:48] Marcus: acceptance criteria — let's list them now so we can sync later. propose: 1) p50 <200ms and p95 <700ms for 50 qps sustained, 2) pass spike test with graceful degradation (no errors >1%), 3) audit logs retained 12 months and delivered to Splunk, 4) SAML + SCIM working for test Okta tenant, 5) SOC2 summary provided and ISO control mapping reviewed.
[04:22] Jordan: yes that's reasonable. we'll draft a pass/fail spreadsheet. Also we'll include a quality gate: minimal semantic regression vs your current model (we'll use a small eval set you provide).
[04:38] Aisha: about SOC2 — we need at least SOC2 Type II report or an on-demand SOC2 summary. can you share a redacted report?
[04:46] Priya: we can share a SOC2 Type II summary and mapping to our controls; full report requires an NDA in some cases. we'll attach the compliance pack and an ISO mapping doc.
[04:58] Nina: regarding SSO testing — we'll need a short window where devs can sign in and we can validate RBAC mapping; can you provide a staging console url?
[05:06] Evan: yes, we'll spin up a staging tenant for the pilot and provide a staging console and API key management. for SAML we'll provide metadata and a test SP/IDP flow.
[05:18] Leo: benchmarks — what tools do you prefer? we use k6 for load, but we can run JMeter too.
[05:23] Priya: k6 is great. we'll provide k6 scripts, a harness README, and sample token distribution. We'll also include a python harness for payload generation. Expect some transcription noise in logs when we capture audio, uh I mean when we capture traces.
[05:38] Marcus: timeline — we'd like pilot running in two weeks and final acceptance within 6 weeks.
[05:43] Jordan: two weeks to start sounds tight but doable. proposed timeline: week 0: setup SAML, share SOC2/ISO docs, week 1: deploy dedicated pilot in eu-west-1 and run bench baseline, week 2: spike tests and quality evals, week 3-4: iterate, then formal acceptance. so 4-6 week runway to full acceptance.
[06:05] Aisha: any legal/contract asks for data residency? we'll need a DPA addendum and SCCs.
[06:11] Jordan: we already have a DPA template and can add SCCs if required. For Private deployments we can do more strict language.
[06:19] Nina: who will run the bench? Redwood or HalcyonWare?
[06:23] Priya: we can run jointly. Redwood will run the first baseline and share the harness; HalcyonWare will run the representative payloads. results shared to the spreadsheet.
[06:33] Marcus: sample acceptance test: run 1 hour at 50 qps with your recommended model, measure p50/p95, collect GPU util, token cost estimate, and assert no PII in logged prompts.
[06:47] Evan: For cost estimate we'll include token accounting and recommended quantization for Dedicated to reduce per-token cost. We'll also show fallback policies: if Dedicated saturation occurs we can route to a cheaper hosted variant with slightly higher latency but lower cost.
[06:58] Leo: logging — we need request IDs to correlate app logs with inference logs. can you surface request-id in headers?
[07:04] Priya: yes we include request-id in responses and store it in audit logs as correlation id. we'll show a sample log line in the compliance pack.
[07:13] Aisha: redaction — please show how you mask PII before storing full prompt.
[07:18] Evan: we have configurable redaction rules and integrated regex filters; default pilot config redacts likely PII. We'll show how to test redaction during bench.
[07:30] Jordan: ok next steps recap: I'll send SOC2/ISO docs and pilot quote. Priya will send bench harness. Nina will provide Okta metadata. Leo to share payloads. We'll schedule the benchmark window week of Jan 25.
[07:46] Marcus: sounds good. any blockers?
[07:49] Aisha: NDA for full SOC2 report might be required but not a blocker.
[07:53] Jordan: great — thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the shared spreadsheet and links.
[07:58] Meeting end.

Notes: Transcript has natural stutters and occasional mis-heard words ("Redwood Dedi" for Redwood Dedicated, "sock two" for SOC2 in one auto-gen line). Links shared in chat: compliance pack (https://redwood.example.com/packs/compliance-halcyon), bench harness repo (https://github.com/redwood-infra/poc-bench-harness), pricing quote draft (link sent in follow-up email).
